title: Localizing quantum information
abstract: The idea that information can be localized is pervasive in physics. In thermodynamics, entropy flows from one reservoir to another, and in quantum gravity, the entropy content of some spatial regions is bounded. In quantum information theory, information is transmitted from one place to another, and entanglement can provide an advantage when there are constraints on such transmission.   Shannon entropy quantifies localizable information in the sense that marginalization defines an outer measure on the set of parts of a classical multipartite system. In contrast, von Neumann entropy does not quantify localizable information in this sense. However, a variant of von Neumann entropy, which originates in noncommutative geometry, does.   We prove that this adjusted von Neumann entropy is the minimum quantum entropy that quantifies localizable information. We also prove that this is the unique quantum entropy that characterizes Bell states in terms of redundant information, directly generalizing the classical case. We work with finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras throughout, modeling finite quantum systems that may have superselection sectors.
summary: This paper develops a novel quantum entropy, the adjusted von Neumann entropy ($	ilde{S}$), designed to correctly quantify 'localizable information' in quantum systems, unlike the standard von Neumann entropy. The authors prove that $	ilde{S}$ is the unique entropy satisfying key physical constraints, and they use it to provide a definitive characterization of entangled Bell states. This advances the foundational understanding of information measures in quantum theory.
main_problem: The paper seeks to define a quantum entropy measure that accurately quantifies 'localizable information' in quantum systems, a property that standard von Neumann entropy lacks.
main_result: The authors prove that an adjusted von Neumann entropy, $	ilde{S}$, is the minimum quantum entropy satisfying the localizability monotonicity condition and uniquely characterizes Bell states.
method: The analysis involves comparing the axioms of classical Shannon entropy with quantum entropy measures using finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras and establishing necessary and sufficient conditions via algebraic constraints.
model_or_system: The study models finite quantum systems using finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras, $A$, which can possess superselection sectors. The focus is on bipartite systems described by states $ho \in A \otimes B$.
key_observables: Adjusted von Neumann entropy ($	ilde{S}$), Shannon entropy, and the characterization of Bell states.
important_parameters: The dimension of the system ($n$), which dictates the additive constant in the adjusted entropy ($\log n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras, and the definition of $	ilde{S}$ requires an additive correction to standard von Neumann entropy to achieve localizability.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the failure of standard von Neumann entropy to quantify localizable information, then proposing and proving the properties of the adjusted entropy $	ilde{S}$ based on monotonicity, and finally using $	ilde{S}$ to provide a structural characterization of Bell states.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, information-theoretic tool ($	ilde{S}$) to distinguish physically meaningful entropy measures from mathematically defined ones, which is crucial for understanding entanglement and information flow in quantum systems.
